reasoning: The deepseek model successfully audited all files, including the PKGBUILD, and found no malicious code. The qwen model's 'inconclusive' verdict was solely due to transient API errors (HTTP 400) when auditing inert files (LICENSE and .nvchecker.toml). The PKGBUILD follows standard AUR practices for a -git package, fetching a zip snapshot from the official upstream GitHub repository. The use of SKIP for checksums and curl/jq in pkgver() are normal, necessary patterns for VCS packages using zip snapshots and do not constitute an injection risk.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is an artifact of transient API errors in the qwen model, which failed to audit two non-executable files (LICENSE and .nvchecker.toml), resulting in an overall 'inconclusive' status. The deepseek model successfully audited all files and found them safe. There is no substantive disagreement on the security merits of the code.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .nvchecker.toml and LICENSE due to HTTP 400 API errors
learnings: Transient API errors on inert files (like LICENSE or TOML configs) should not force an overall 'inconclusive' verdict if the executable files (PKGBUILD) are successfully audited and found safe. The audit tool should differentiate between missing critical executable files and failed audits of non-executable metadata.
The judge logic should be able to override 'inconclusive' verdicts caused by partial tool errors on non-executable files when the PKGBUILD is verified safe and no suspicious files were skipped.
